status: Original source-fit task protocols for independent review; no child observations or efficacy study
coverageMeaning: Authoring coverage and component associations are distinct from whole-topic mastery and learner attainment. Every specifically required source performance remains an actual task, not assumed from a proxy.

protocols.title: Deliberate pressure and mark effects
protocols.task: Offer comfortable suitable tools and surfaces. Invite a chosen light, dark or differently covered mark, then ask for a deliberately changed effect. Try another available tool or surface without prescribing one grip or handedness.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner starts, moves and stops deliberately, changes movement or pressure for the intended mark, and adjusts handling for a new tool. A showing or pointing explanation is valid.
protocols.nearMiss: Accidental traces, naming a colour, tracing only the adult line, or producing the same mark while merely saying it is different does not demonstrate deliberate adjustment.
protocols.transfer: Ask for a chosen effect on another safe surface; observe an adjusted action rather than requiring the same pressure on every material.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Own visual choices with available materials
protocols.task: Provide safe varied drawing, painting and modelling materials with meaningful choices of working area and amounts. Let the learner choose an idea, explore material effects, make an own work, compare alternatives and alter one visual relation. Repeat with a smaller or larger available working area or changed material supply.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual choices about line, form, colour, texture and placement serve the learner’s stated or shown intention; material exploration changes the work. Available area and material limits are handled practically.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming materials, filling an adult-designed template, describing an imaginary work, or changing paper size without adapting the arrangement does not show the complete operation.
protocols.transfer: Offer a new theme or material/area limit and ask the learner to choose and revise a new arrangement. No mathematical scale ratio, realism or adult taste criterion is added.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Separate flat and spatial making panels
protocols.task: Include an actual flat visual work and an actual spatial work. Use available paper/card, safe found materials or suitable modelling material. The learner makes intentional arrangements in each, changes a relation and checks the practical result; spatial work is actually constructed and viewed from more than one position.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The flat work and spatial work each contain learner choices; the spatial assembly has real arranged parts rather than merely a photograph or drawing of a model.
protocols.nearMiss: A flat shape puzzle, a copied diagram, or an adult-built model cannot stand for the learner making an own spatial artwork.
protocols.transfer: Change available materials or viewing position and ask for a deliberate new arrangement. Stable/safe handling is checked without importing engineering load calculations.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Material combination with an own arrangement
protocols.task: Offer safe materials that differ in texture, colour and workable consistency. For collage, the learner chooses, arranges and joins actual materials on a surface. For assemblage, the learner combines found materials in a real spatial artwork. Record which source panel is required and perform it, including both where the record calls for the broader portfolio.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner chooses contrasting or related materials, makes an own arrangement, uses a suitable safe join and changes a relationship for an intended effect.
protocols.nearMiss: Only sorting ready-made textures, gluing every piece exactly where an adult has marked, or substituting a photo for actual spatial assembly does not meet the making duty.
protocols.transfer: Change one available material or amount and ask for another deliberate arrangement and safe workable combination.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Actual decorative arrangement and separate pattern reasoning
protocols.task: Use safe available loose or attached materials to make an own decorative arrangement. Where a repeating pattern is chosen, have the learner create its rule, continue it and explain the repeating unit. Separately ask what visual arrangement they intended and invite a purposeful change.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The artwork has deliberate placement and an actual chosen pattern where required. The mathematical component checks continuing, describing and creating object-pattern rules rather than inferring them from an attractive result.
protocols.nearMiss: Copying adult placements without an own pattern decision, or declaring any scattered decoration to be a repeating rule, is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use new materials with the same rule, then choose a different visual arrangement. Formal complexity and aesthetic taste are not mastery criteria.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Produce texture by changing one material
protocols.task: Choose one suitable safe material, such as paper or clay, and let the learner make two contrasting surface effects by changing how it is worked. Incorporate a chosen texture into an own artwork and compare the actual results by appropriate touch or viewing.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The same declared material is manipulated to produce contrasting textures, and the learner selects or changes an effect for the work.
protocols.nearMiss: Only sorting two pre-textured objects, changing to a different material, or naming rough/smooth without producing the effects does not close this source position.
protocols.transfer: Invite another texture using a different safe action on the same material, then adapt the action on another suitable material without demanding the same outcome.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Voice, body, role and space exploration
protocols.task: Provide actual linked opportunities in voice/music, dramatic role-play and dance/movement. The learner explores sounds, body actions, space and safe objects, creates a short expressive idea, tries an alternative and performs it. Record the separate panels, with available access supports.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual vocal output, role/action and chosen movement are demonstrated. Ideas and emotions may be fictional; no personal disclosure or forced emotional display is needed.
protocols.nearMiss: An instrumental-only pattern, a drawing of a dancer, a script recited without action, or adult interpretation of a learner’s mood does not establish all panels.
protocols.transfer: Change the imagined situation or available space and invite a new expressive choice in each required panel.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Audible making, listening and purposeful musical revision
protocols.task: Offer the source-required opportunities for voice, body sounds, suitable instruments and safe everyday sound objects. The learner makes an own short audible response to a familiar song, event or chosen intention, listens to it and changes timing, sound/silence, quality, contrast or ending for that intention. Record the actual channels used rather than treating them as interchangeable proof.
protocols.positiveEvidence: There is an actual sounded work, an audible purposeful revision and an adaptation to a changed intention or available sound source. Repetition or a nonperiodic sequence can both be valid.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming an imagined sound, copying a fixed adult pattern, explaining vibration physics or generating a formal AB rule does not establish musical listening and shaping.
protocols.transfer: Change the available sound source or intended contrast and ask the learner to make, listen and revise again. No taste, formal complexity or professional performance norm is imposed.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Repeat, vary and coordinate an actual rhythm
protocols.task: Use a familiar age-appropriate chant or song and actual clapping, tapping or suitable sound sources. Replicate a beat and repeated sound pattern, then make a purposeful variation. Where the source specifies slow/medium timing or a familiar rhythmic case, demonstrate those actual contrasts within a comfortable range.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner joins repeated sounds at the right moment, keeps the selected beat and makes an audible variation that can be compared with the first version.
protocols.nearMiss: Only reciting tempo words, moving randomly near music or showing a mathematical pattern on paper does not establish rhythmic performance.
protocols.transfer: Use a new short chant or changed comfortable tempo; keep listening and joining at the appropriate moments rather than merely repeating identical actions.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Heard pitch and contextual loudness
protocols.task: Provide a comfortable sounded reference and let the learner respond with voice or a suitable pitched source, listen to the comparison and try an adjustment. Use a new reference. For the source position requiring voice changes for a composition, space or occasion, include an actual vocal case with BOTH pitch and loudness adapted to that case. Retain a source position that asks for an attempt as an attempt, not a silently upgraded success norm.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The reference is actually heard and an intentional pitched response is actually made. For the broader vocal case, pitch and loudness both change appropriately to the declared purpose; whole matching-topic assessment additionally checks comparison and adjustment across new references.
protocols.nearMiss: A louder response alone, naming high/low without producing sound, copying a rhythm or explaining string vibration is not pitch reproduction. Instrumental-only output does not establish a specifically vocal duty.
protocols.transfer: Offer a new comfortable reference and another appropriate space or expressive purpose. Do not impose absolute-note naming, fixed concert tuning or adult vocal range.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Artistic timing with sound and action
protocols.task: In a short musical or dramatic situation, deliberately try different lengths of sound and silence and different lengths of movement and stillness. Compare the versions and select one for an intended effect, with a supported safe seated/standing action option.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner actually makes and compares audible and visible timing choices and uses a chosen pause or stillness within the work.
protocols.nearMiss: Sitting quietly because told to, holding still for a universal quota, or talking about silence without performing it is not artistic timing.
protocols.transfer: Change the scene or musical intention and ask for a different timing choice, explaining or showing its effect.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: More than one expressive approach
protocols.task: Choose a familiar or invented idea and make two distinct artistic versions using the source-required visual or performing form. Let the learner decide what to vary, enact each version and compare how it serves the intention. A story adaptation must really alter a character, setting or ending, with the familiar original understood.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner contributes actual own ideas and changes an expressive approach rather than only changing a label. An imagined feeling is legitimate without claiming it describes the learner’s current mood.
protocols.nearMiss: Two exact adult copies, merely saying “another idea”, or judging only whether the learner looks enthusiastic does not show creative variation.
protocols.transfer: Use another theme or a new constraint and invite a new independently chosen alternative. Source illustrations are examples, not a required inventory of animals, masks or props.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Manageable artistic challenge and resources
protocols.task: During a genuine manageable making/performance task, invite an own plan, selection and gathering of available resources, checking of the result and a different approach when the first does not work. Use an actually encountered challenge rather than deliberately causing frustration.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner checks an outcome, identifies a real difficulty, tries a substantively different action and uses or seeks suitable resources. Keep the whole existing planning/checking/help/strategy evidence separate from a single artwork.
protocols.nearMiss: Merely remaining seated, repeating an unsuccessful action unchanged, smiling or having an adult finish the work is not independent persistence or strategy change.
protocols.transfer: Use another manageable task or available-resource change. A learner may be frustrated while acting constructively; no pleasant-mood or never-ask-for-help rule is inferred.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Own reasoned response and another legitimate perspective
protocols.task: View or hear actual appropriate artworks/performances and the learner’s own work. Attend to the source-relevant theme, details, material qualities, space and situation. Ask for an own response with an observable reason and invite a different legitimate peer response; listen and respond to that actual view.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner points to or describes features supporting a response and acknowledges that another person can respond differently. Making and viewing are both sampled where the source requires both.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming colours, repeating the adult’s opinion, praising everything, or assuming disagreement means a peer is wrong is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Offer another work or arrangement with a contrasting plausible response. No universal emotion-colour code, correct taste or mandatory enjoyment is scored.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Attributed local arts encounter
protocols.task: Prepare accessible, accurate, age-appropriate local artworks, recordings, images or a supported practitioner encounter, with source/community/style attribution checked. Offer actual looking/listening and voluntary exploration/questions about materials, practices or context. Provide needed background rather than presuming a family tradition.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The task provides a real local-cultural arts encounter, accurate attribution and space for the learner’s own response or interest. A quiet response or preference for another work is not a mastery failure.
protocols.nearMiss: A culture stereotype, a falsely attributed image, compulsory praise, a forced personal/religious disclosure or a fixed artist-name quiz cannot stand for this source duty.
protocols.transfer: Provide another accurately attributed local example and invite similarities, differences or an optional question; recognise more than one legitimate response.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Actual shared making and response
protocols.task: Undertake a real joint artwork or performance in the source-named or selected form. Each learner contributes an idea, listens to another idea, builds on it and completes a fair agreed part. Include discussion of own thoughts/responses during the work, not only after an unrelated game.
protocols.positiveEvidence: An own idea and another idea are visible in the shared process; the learner actually completes their part and responds to another contribution. Turn-taking and listening are checked directly.
protocols.nearMiss: A solo product beside someone else, repeating an adult plan, generic sociability or a peer doing all production does not establish collaborative artistic work.
protocols.transfer: Change a role, partner or resource and repeat genuine shared planning/making with a fair contribution.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Actual songs, rhythms and ensemble coordination
protocols.task: Use accurately introduced appropriate songs and rhythmic material with available safe vocal/instrumental resources. Prepare a declared varied portfolio including actual singing and actual rhythm performance; include individual work and a duet/group/ensemble arrangement as appropriate to the printed source. Rehearse, listen and coordinate starts, entries and endings. For the specific partner-alignment position, check volume, pitch AND tempo in the shared actual performance.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner actually sings and performs rhythms, contributes to the selected arrangements and adjusts to partners. The partner-alignment task explicitly samples loudness, pitched output and timing rather than assuming one establishes the others.
protocols.nearMiss: Only an instrumental recording, one solo clap, sharing equipment nicely or recognising instrument names cannot prove singing, varied arrangements or ensemble alignment.
protocols.transfer: Change the comfortable song/rhythm or one partner entry and coordinate again; do not require one national song, language, instrument or professional accuracy norm.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Sequence attention across required performance panels
protocols.task: Prepare short accessible role-play, music and dance/movement sequences. The learner knows the selected order, rehearses actual parts, attends to cues and performs them with peers. Record each required panel rather than replacing all with a single genre.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner follows and contributes to the actual sequence in each required form, notices relevant cues and coordinates a changed entry or order.
protocols.nearMiss: Only arranging picture cards, acting once while a recording supplies all music, or doing a solo unsequenced action cannot close cross-form sequence attention.
protocols.transfer: Change an entry or short sequence and perform again in the required panels, without introducing a reading, notation or complex choreography gate.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Own practised expressive movement
protocols.task: Use a safe available space and accessible seated or standing movement options. The learner chooses an everyday or imagined idea, combines actions into an own sequence, practises, performs and changes a visible quality or spatial relationship intentionally. Include partner/group or source-specified movement style only where the source calls for it.
protocols.positiveEvidence: There is actual chosen movement, a coherent sequence, practice and purposeful contrast or revision. The learner can show the intended difference without a compulsory verbal explanation.
protocols.nearMiss: Random vigorous motion, copying a teacher’s entire routine, a static drawn dancer, balancing alone or clapping a beat alone is not own expressive sequence creation.
protocols.transfer: Change the imagined action, available space or intended movement quality and adapt the sequence; no spins, athletic norms, fixed gender roles or prescribed emotion gestures are required.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Primary whole-claim theatre portfolio
protocols.task: Use short age-appropriate script and poem panels plus an improvised scene. The learner helps shape a role or situation, rehearses and actually performs with intonation, tone, volume, pace, meaningful silence/stillness and action. Explore a changed character response in improvisation and alter a familiar story where that component is tagged. Include safe space/props and explicit language/meaning choices, without requiring independent script reading.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual script AND poem performances, an improvised new response and purposeful voice/action/timing are present. The learner makes decisions about meaning/impact rather than only repeating adult lines.
protocols.nearMiss: A flat retelling, one freeze pose, a copied gesture or adult-supplied recording cannot establish the whole existing scripts-and-poetry claim. A single scene is only one component check.
protocols.transfer: Change the audience intention, character situation or poem phrasing and rehearse an adjusted performance. No compulsory personal trauma disclosure or stereotyped role is used.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Source-accurate musical comparison
protocols.task: Introduce at least two appropriate, accurately attributed musical examples used in the class. With actual listening, compare tempo/Laya, rhythm or rhythmic cycle/Taala, heard pitch/Sur, expressive feeling/Bhaava, lyrics and performed expression. Supply style-specific explanations and translated meanings where needed. Compare versions or short excerpts through listening, optional safe singing/playing and reasoned response.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner identifies audible similarities/differences in each source-relevant dimension and connects an expressive interpretation to heard features or supplied lyric meaning. Different supported responses can coexist.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming fast/slow alone, classifying only sound-making physics, insisting every culture uses one scale or emotion code, or guessing lyrics in an unknown language does not close the comparison.
protocols.transfer: Use a new accurately contextualised excerpt and justify a comparison. The task is primary listening/experimentation, not notation analysis, expert Raaga identification or a universal feeling score.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Observed movement features and expressive choices
protocols.task: Introduce appropriate accurately attributed movement examples actually taught or viewed in class. Compare movement, rhythm, posture, theme and expression using observation and safe selected movement trials. Separate observed features from a personal interpretation.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner points to real contrasting movement features and relates a chosen interpretation to the observed sequence, without treating one gesture as a universal code.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming a dance, clapping its beat, judging athletic difficulty or guessing a culture from costume does not establish the required comparisons.
protocols.transfer: Offer another introduced example and compare a real movement quality or arrangement while acknowledging different plausible responses.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Compare classroom dramatic choices
protocols.task: View or participate in actual appropriate classroom dramatic works. Compare themes and selected role, situation, space, voice, action, timing or prop choices, and discuss how those choices affect a supported response. Allow showing a changed line/action as evidence.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner identifies actual dramatic elements and a meaningful similarity/difference with a reason grounded in the performances.
protocols.nearMiss: Only retelling the plot, naming one role or saying a work is good without a performance-based reason is incomplete.
protocols.transfer: Change a dramatic choice in a short scene and compare the resulting meaning/impact without requiring expert theatre history.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Compare actual visual elements and themes
protocols.task: Use actual classroom artworks and accurately introduced accessible examples. Compare line, form, colour, placement/space, texture and theme in the relevant works. Let the learner show how changing an arrangement alters their own intended effect.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The response identifies observable visual decisions and thematic similarities/differences with reasons, rather than merely listing material names.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming colours, guessing the artist’s private feelings, equating realism with quality or praising every work is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Provide another work or changed arrangement and justify an observed comparison. No universal aesthetic ranking is required.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Choose, use and review form-specific processes
protocols.task: For the source-named or school-selected form, provide safe usable resources and genuine choices. Visual work includes actual material/tool/technique choices; music includes actual voices/instruments/arrangements; movement includes actual action/costume/prop or arrangement choices as relevant; theatre includes actual role/space/prop or production choices. Plan, try, review/rehearse and present an own contribution.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner chooses and actually uses a relevant process or resource, can show its effect and participates in rehearsal or review. Music-selection and rehearsal participation remain actual duties where printed.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming instruments/materials, describing an adult-completed work or expressing a preference without any relevant production/rehearsal contribution does not show process familiarity.
protocols.transfer: Change an available resource or presentation condition and choose a workable adaptation, with no invented expensive-tool or advanced-technique gate.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Observe natural features and use an artistic interpretation
protocols.task: Use a safe direct observation or accurate recording/image of a natural setting. In visual work notice form/line/colour/texture; in music notice audible qualities, pace/pattern and expressive possibilities; in movement notice actions/qualities; in theatre notice a context or imagined situation. Describe observed features and make or show an artistic response in the relevant selected form.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner identifies an actual natural feature and describes a defensible artistic quality or possible use, distinguishing observation from an invented artistic interpretation.
protocols.nearMiss: A physics explanation alone, naming an animal without observing it, claiming animals have human motives as fact, or assigning one universal emotion to a natural sound is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use another natural example and choose a new artistic response. No vibration explanation, ecosystem course or belief about natural beauty is a prerequisite.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Low-stakes contextual engagement channel
protocols.task: Offer an accessible artistic choice with preparation, optional sharing and time to explore. Invite a low-stakes reflection on what felt possible, interesting, uncertain or worthwhile in this particular task. Record opportunities and source-specific contextual requirements separately from actual production evidence.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The task design provides voluntary exploration, voice and support. The learner may show interest through action or a quiet response; confidence or enjoyment can vary over time and coexist with difficulty.
protocols.nearMiss: Forced enthusiasm, smiling as a pass condition, absence of tears, compliance with every activity or an adult inferring a private feeling is not valid mastery evidence.
protocols.transfer: Offer another supported choice and an optional reflection. No binary new affect score, diagnosis or claim that a learner has permanently acquired enjoyment is made.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Complete foundational Arts portfolio
protocols.task: Compose the visual making, flat/spatial, integrated performing, imaginative variation, actual collaboration, response and attributed local-arts protocols. Use real tasks across the formal stage, with stage-end reference rather than demanding every operation at the youngest age. Retain joy/engagement as the separate low-stakes contextual channel.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The portfolio actually samples every required child duty in its relevant form and provides opportunities for own making and response. The broad goal is independently judged from that complete portfolio, not inferred from a sum of linked topic labels.
protocols.nearMiss: Only one finished artwork, one music pattern, pleasant participation or a complete list of child codes does not demonstrate the broad goal.
protocols.transfer: A changed theme/material/partner shows adaptation in the relevant panels while retaining every original performance condition.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: Goal-specific complete form portfolio
protocols.task: For the exact LS1 form and printed goal, compose the two child-competency protocols with all required production, response, resource and contextual panels. For the human-experience goal include an actually expressed everyday or fictional human experience, without forced personal disclosure. For creative goals include actual own generative choices beyond imitation. For the surroundings/local-arts goal include both actual natural observation and an attributed local-arts encounter. Independently compare the complete portfolio with the broad goal and retain any confidence/interest channel separately.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The declared form and goal have complete child-task closure, with actual making/performance and no missing response/material duties. Formal LS1 resource conditions are recorded.
protocols.nearMiss: A single child task, a count of source codes or substituting a different art form does not establish the goal.
protocols.transfer: Use a changed meaningful situation in the same selected form; no unqualified transfer to all other forms or different resource provision is asserted.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.

protocols.title: School-form-bound integrated baseline
protocols.task: Declare the school’s appropriate accessible selected forms from the visual and performing arts, supplied resources and source-relevant variety. Compose actual own creation/presentation, practical material/process familiarity, collaboration and own/other response tasks within those forms. Provide separate optional engagement reflection for the broad goal. Form-specific candidates stay conditional until that binding; no national form selection is requested.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The design accounts for every baseline source position with a concrete parameterised portfolio and explicit selection/resources. Only genuinely form-independent required components receive unconditional flat associations.
protocols.nearMiss: Turning sound, dance and theatre alternatives into simultaneous universal mastery requirements, dropping the source position, or using one instrumental pattern for every performance duty is invalid.
protocols.transfer: Change a resource or selected example within the declared school programme and adapt the actual portfolio. A different school selection requires rebinding, not inferred mastery transfer.
protocols.coverageMeaning: Original, untested authoring protocol. Actual source duties and whole-topic assessment remain distinct; no observation or learner attainment is asserted.
